`\",\"` without a following space does not split.\n- Ties in event count are broken by region name in byte order, not locale or case-insensitive order.\n- No region row is hardcoded; all values come from the file read.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Near.md ===\n# FEATURE: Near\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The `near` report: events within a haversine great-circle distance of a point, nearest first. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MagFilter.md, FEATURE-Formatting.md, FEATURE-Options.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes near, haversine_km |\n| Consumes    | read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, format_time, format_mag, format_decimal, parse_args |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes near --lat <deg> --lon <deg> --radius <km> [--min-mag <m>] <file>` lists the events whose distance from a point is at most the radius.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line. `--lat`, `--lon`, and `--radius` are all required. `parse_args` enforces `--lat` in -90..90, `--lon` in -180..180, and `--radius` greater than zero; any violation or omission is a usage error (exit 2).\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. `read_feed`, `extract_events`, and `filter_events` produce the kept events.\n2. `haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)` is a pure function on a sphere of radius 6371.0 km, with angles in radians:\n   `h = sin^2((lat2 - lat1) / 2) + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin^2((lon2 - lon1) / 2)` and `d = 2 * 6371.0 * asin(sqrt(h))`. Event coordinates are `[longitude, latitude, depth_km]`.\n3. `compute_near(events, lat, lon, radius)` keeps events whose unrounded distance is `<= radius` and orders them by unrounded distance ascending, then by event time ascending.\n4. `write_csv` writes the report, with `distance_km` rounded half up to one decimal.\n\n## Output\n\nHeader: `distance_km,time,mag,place,id`. One row per matching event: distance with one decimal, UTC time, magnitude with one decimal, place, id. An event at exactly the radius is included. No matches yields only the header with exit 0. Places containing commas are quoted by the `csv` module; non-ASCII places are UTF-8.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line.\n\n## Writes\n\nStandard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC near-haversine-distance-and-radius ===\nIntent: Reported distances match an independent haversine on a 6371.0 km sphere, and only events within the radius are listed, nearest first.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport tempfile\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dphi = p2 - p1\n    dlam = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin(dphi / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dlam / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))\n\n\norigin = (27.72, 85.32)\npoints = [\n    (\"far\", 35.68, 139.69),\n    (\"mid\", 28.60, 87.37),\n    (\"near1\", 28.80, 87.13),\n    (\"near2\", 28.50, 87.35),\n]\nfeatures = []\nfor i, (name, lat, lon) in enumerate(points):\n    features.append({\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0 + i / 10, \"place\": \"Place \" + name, \"time\": 1736200000000 + i * 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, 10.0]},\n        \"id\": name,\n    })\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\ndist = {name: hav(origin[0], origin[1], lat, lon) for name, lat, lon in points}\nradius = round(sorted(dist.values())[2] + 1.0, 1)\ninside = sorted([n for n in dist if dist[n] <= radius], key=lambda n: dist[n])\nassert 0 < len(inside) < len(points)\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump(doc, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\n        \"near\", \"--lat\", str(origin[0]), \"--lon\", str(origin[1]), \"--radius\", str(radius), path\n    )\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"distance_km\", \"time\", \"mag\", \"place\", \"id\"]\nassert [r[4] for r in rows[1:]] == inside\nfor r in rows[1:]:\n    assert abs(float(r[0]) - dist[r[4]]) <= 0.051\n=== END AC ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- The earth radius is exactly 6371.0 km; no other radius or formula is used.\n- The radius test compares the unrounded distance; only the printed value is rounded.\n- An event at exactly the radius is included (`<=`).\n- No distance or row is hardcoded; all values are computed from the file and the arguments.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Fetch.md ===\n# FEATURE: Fetch\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The `fetch` command: download a USGS date range as GeoJSON and save the response unchanged to a file. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-Options.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md, FEATURE-FeedValidation.md |\n| Provides    | quakes fetch, build_url, http_get |\n| Consumes    | parse_args, read_feed |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes fetch --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --end <YYYY-MM-DD> [--min-mag <m>] --out <file>` saves a period of the USGS event feed so the report commands can read it.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line. `--start`, `--end`, and `--out` are required; `--min-mag` defaults to `2.5`. A missing required option, an unlisted option, or any positional argument is a usage error (exit 2) and no HTTP call is made.\n\n## Module layout\n\nCode lives in `cli/fetch.py`:\n\n- `build_url(start, end, min_mag) -> str` returns `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query` with query parameters `format=geojson`, `starttime=<start>`, `endtime=<end>`, `minmagnitude=<min_mag>`, `orderby=time-asc`. `min_mag` is the text given on the command line (or `2.5`).\n- `http_get(url) -> tuple[int, bytes]` is the single replaceable network function. It calls `urllib.request.urlopen` through attribute access on the `urllib.request` module (so a test can patch `urllib.request.urlopen`), returns the HTTP status and body bytes, and is the only function in the product that opens a connection.\n- The command handler calls `http_get` through the module global (`cli.fetch.http_get`) so tests can replace it.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Build the URL and call `http_get(url)`.\n2. Validate: status 200, body parses as JSON, and is an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a list `features` (reusing the `read_feed` validation rules on the body).\n3. Only after validation, write the body bytes unchanged (binary write) to `--out`.\n4. Write `fetched,<count>` to standard output, where `<count>` is the number of features.\n\nFailure handling is specified in FEATURE-FetchFailure.md.\n\n## Output\n\nStandard output is exactly one CSV line `fetched,<count>`; exit 0. The saved file is byte-for-byte the response body.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe USGS FDSN event web service over HTTPS.\n\n## Writes\n\nThe file named by `--out`, and standard output.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC fetch-saves-body-unchanged ===\nIntent: fetch writes the response body byte for byte to --out and prints fetched with the feature count; the HTTP call is stubbed.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nfeatures = [\n    {\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.1, \"place\": \"Awash, Ethiopia\", \"time\": 1735706358208, \"tsunami\": 0},\n     \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [40.0, 9.0, 10]}, \"id\": \"a\" + str(i)}\n    for i in range(3)\n]\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, indent=3, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\") + b\"\\n\\n\"\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert stub.call_count == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == body\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows == [[\"fetched\", str(len(features))]]\n=== END AC fetch-saves-body-unchanged ===\n\n=== AC fetch-request-url ===\nIntent: The request goes to the USGS FDSN query endpoint with the GeoJSON format, the given dates, the default minimum magnitude, and time ascending order.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.parse\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 0\n    url = stub.call_args[0][0]\nparts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)\nquery = urllib.parse.parse_qs(parts.query)\nassert parts.scheme == \"https\"\nassert parts.netloc == \"earthquake.usgs.gov\"\nassert parts.path == \"/fdsnws/event/1/query\"\nassert query[\"format\"] == [\"geojson\"]\nassert query[\"starttime\"] == [start]\nassert query[\"endtime\"] == [end]\nassert query[\"minmagnitude\"] == [\"2.5\"]\nassert query[\"orderby\"] == [\"time-asc\"]\n=== END AC fetch-request-url ===\n\n=== AC fetch-min-mag-passthrough ===\nIntent: An explicit --min-mag value is sent as minmagnitude, and build_url builds the same query directly.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.parse\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.fetch import build_url\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nstart = \"2025-02-01\"\nend = \"2025-02-03\"\nmin_mag = \"4.5\"\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\n            \"fetch\", \"--min-mag\", min_mag, \"--end\", end, \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out_path\n        )\n    assert code == 0\n    url = stub.call_args[0][0]\nquery = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).query)\nassert query[\"minmagnitude\"] == [min_mag]\nassert query[\"starttime\"] == [start]\nassert query[\"endtime\"] == [end]\ndirect = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(build_url(start, end, min_mag)).query)\nassert direct == query\n=== END AC fetch-min-mag-passthrough ===\n\n=== AC fetch-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Missing required options, an unlisted option, or an extra positional argument exit 2, make no HTTP call, and write no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    cases = [\n        (\"fetch\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--out\", out_path),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path, \"extra\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path, \"--n\", \"3\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", \"--out\", out_path),\n    ]\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, b\"{}\")) as stub:\n        for args in cases:\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(*args)\n            assert code == 2, args\n            assert out == \"\", args\n        assert stub.call_count == 0\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-usage-errors ===\n\n=== AC fetch-http-get-uses-urllib ===\nIntent: http_get returns the status and body from urllib.request.urlopen, which is stubbed so no network connection is opened.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.fetch import http_get\n\npayload = b\"payload bytes\"\nstatus = 200\n\n\nclass FakeResponse:\n    def __init__(self, code, data):\n        self.status = code\n        self._data = data\n\n    def read(self):\n        return self._data\n\n    def getcode(self):\n        return self.status\n\n    def __enter__(self):\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *exc):\n        return False\n\n\nwith mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", return_value=FakeResponse(status, payload)) as opener:\n    got_status, got_body = http_get(\"https://example.invalid/query\")\nassert opener.call_count == 1\nassert got_status == status\nassert got_body == payload\n=== END AC fetch-http-get-uses-urllib ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Tests never open a network connection; every fetch test replaces `cli.fetch.http_get` or `urllib.request.urlopen`.\n- The saved file is the response body unchanged: no re-serialization, re-encoding, or newline translation.\n- The output file is written only after the response is validated.\n- Only the `fetch` command touches the network; report commands never do.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-FetchFailure.md ===\n# FEATURE: Fetch Failure\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Failure behavior of `fetch`: network, HTTP, and body errors exit 1 and never write or alter a file. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-Fetch.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | fetch failure handling |\n| Consumes    | http_get |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nWhen the download cannot produce a valid GeoJSON FeatureCollection, `fetch` reports an operational failure and leaves the filesystem exactly as it found it.\n\n## Trigger\n\nAny of the following during `quakes fetch` (after arguments parse successfully):\n\n- a network error (any `urllib.error.URLError`, `OSError`, or timeout from the HTTP layer);\n- an HTTP status other than 200;\n- a 200 body that is not JSON, or is JSON but not an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a list `features`.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- `http_get` returns `(status, body)` for every HTTP response, including non-200 statuses (an `HTTPError` is converted to its code and body), and raises `OperationalError` for `URLError`, `OSError`, and timeouts.\n- The `fetch` handler also converts any `OSError` raised by a replaced `http_get` into `OperationalError`.\n- A non-200 status or an invalid body raises `OperationalError`.\n- All checks complete before `--out` is opened, so no file is created and a pre-existing file at `--out` keeps its exact bytes.\n- The command exits 1, writes nothing to standard output, and writes one diagnostic line to standard error.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe HTTP response only.\n\n## Writes\n\nStandard error only; never the output file on failure.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-http-status ===\nIntent: A non-200 status exits 1 with empty standard output, one stderr line, and no file written.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nvalid = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nbad_status = 500\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(bad_status, valid)):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-http-status ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-bad-body ===\nIntent: A body that is not JSON, or JSON that is not a FeatureCollection, exits 1 and writes no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nbodies = [\n    b\"this is not json\",\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {}, \"geometry\": None}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": \"nope\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps([1, 2, 3]).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n]\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    for n, body in enumerate(bodies):\n        out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved\" + str(n) + \".geojson\")\n        with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n        assert code == 1, n\n        assert out == \"\", n\n        assert not os.path.exists(out_path), n\n=== END AC fetch-failure-bad-body ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-network-error ===\nIntent: A network error from a stubbed http_get, and a URLError from a patched urlopen, both exit 1 with no file written.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.error\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    first = os.path.join(tmp, \"first.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", side_effect=OSError(\"unreachable\")):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", first)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(first)\n\n    second = os.path.join(tmp, \"second.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", side_effect=urllib.error.URLError(\"no route\")) as opener:\n        code2, out2, err2 = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", second)\n    assert opener.call_count == 1\n    assert code2 == 1\n    assert out2 == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(second)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-network-error ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-http-error-status ===\nIntent: An HTTPError raised by urlopen is treated as a non-200 status, exits 1, and writes no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.error\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nerror = urllib.error.HTTPError(\"https://example.invalid\", 503, \"unavailable\", {}, io.BytesIO(b\"down\"))\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", side_effect=error):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-http-error-status ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-preserves-existing-file ===\nIntent: A failed fetch leaves a pre-existing output file byte-for-byte untouched.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\noriginal = b\"previous contents, not JSON\\n\"\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with open(out_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        fh.write(original)\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(404, b\"missing\")):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == original\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, b\"not json\")):\n        code2, out2, err2 = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code2 == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == original\n=== END AC fetch-failure-preserves-existing-file ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- A failing `fetch` never creates, truncates, or modifies the output file.\n- A failing command writes nothing to standard output and exactly one diagnostic line to standard error; standard error text is never part of a contract.\n- Tests exercise failure only through stubbed HTTP; no test opens a network connection.\n=== END ARTIFACT ==="}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":81543,"cache_read_input_tokens":1568,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":81543},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"961b843c-e48b-4cf9-a8db-c43648e0d6ff","uuid":"5cfccb91-ac04-4347-8114-19c563fd1b3a","timestamp":"2026-10-25T01:11:38.852Z","request_id":"req_011CgN4cJbQpSC11JbToNZsc"}

BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Daily.md ===\n# FEATURE: Daily\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The `daily` report: event count and maximum magnitude per UTC date, followed by a TOTAL row. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MagFilter.md, FEATURE-Formatting.md, FEATURE-Options.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes daily |\n| Consumes    | read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, format_time, format_mag, parse_args |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes daily [--min-mag <m>] <file>` reads a saved USGS GeoJSON file and reports how many events occurred on each UTC date and the strongest magnitude on that date.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line: `./quakes daily [--min-mag <m>] <file>`. The command accepts only `--min-mag`; any other option is a usage error handled by `parse_args`.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. `read_feed(file)` validates and returns the features (`OperationalError`, exit 1, on failure).\n2. `extract_events` drops null-magnitude features.\n3. `filter_events(events, min_mag)` applies `--min-mag`.\n4. `compute_daily(events)` groups events by date, where date is the first 10 characters of `format_time(event.time)`.\n5. Rows are ordered by date ascending (byte order), followed by one `TOTAL` row.\n6. `write_csv` writes the whole report to standard output in one step, after it is fully computed.\n\n`compute_daily(events)` is a pure function returning `(rows, total_row)` with no I/O; formatting is performed by the `format_daily` step that uses `format_mag` and `write_csv`.\n\n## Output\n\nHeader: `date,events,max_mag`.\n\n- One row per date that has at least one event, ascending.\n- `events` is the integer count; `max_mag` is the maximum magnitude with one decimal.\n- Final row: `TOTAL,<events>,<max_mag>` where both values are over all kept events.\n- With no events the output is the header followed by `TOTAL,0,` (empty max).\n- Exit code 0, including the empty case.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line. No other input.\n\n## Writes\n\nStandard output only. Nothing is written to any file.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC daily-groups-by-utc-date ===\nIntent: Events are grouped per UTC date with counts and maximum magnitude, ascending, followed by milli\n\n\ndef feat(i, mag, t):\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": \"10 km N of Town, Land\", \"time\": t, \"tsunami\": 0},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [10.0, 20.0, 5.0]},\n        \"id\": \"e\" + str(i),\n    }\n\n\nspecs = [\n    (5.0, ms(3, 1)),\n    (6.1, ms(1, 2)),\n    (5.4, ms(1, 23, 59, 59, code, out, err = cli_runner(\"daily\", path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"date\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]\nbody = Purpose\n\n`quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>` reports the most active regions in a saved USGS GeoJSON file.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line: `./quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>`. scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\n# (region, mag) pairs supplied as input; the place text is built from the region.\npairs = [\n    (\"Zed\", 5.0), (\"Zed\", 5.6),\n    (\"alpha\", 5.1),\n    (\"Beta\", 5.2), (\"Beta\", 5.0),\n    (\"Gamma\", 5.3), (\"Gamma\", 5.9), (\"Gamma\", 5.1),\n    (\"Delta\", 5.4),\n]\nfeatures = []\nfor i, (region, mag) in enumerate(pairs):\n    features.append({\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": \"12 km N of Town \" + str(i) + \", \" + region,\n                       \"time\": 1735706358208 + i, \"tsunami\": 0},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n        \"id\": \"e\" + str(i),\n    })\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\nexpected = {}\nfor region, mag in pairs:\n    entry = expected.setdefault(region, [0, mag])\n    entry[0] += 1\n    entry[1] = max(entry[1], mag)\norder = sorted(expected, key=lambda r: (-expected[r][0], r))\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump(doc, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]\nassert [r[0] for r in rows[1:]] == order\nfor r in rows[1:]:\n    assert int(r[1]) == expected[r[0]][0]\n    assert float(r[2]) == expected[r[0]][1]\n=== END AC regions-extract-and-order ===\n\n=== AC regions-place-rules ===\nIntent: A place with several commas splits on the last comma-space, a place without one is its own region, and a null place is Unknown.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nthreshold = 5.4\npairs = [(\"Aland\", 5.0), (\"Aland\", 5.4), (\"Bland\", 6.0), (\"Cland\", None), (\"Dland\", 5.3)]\nfeatures = []\nfor i, (region, mag) in enumerate(pairs):\n    features.append({\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": \"5 km S of T, \" + region, \"time\": 1735706358208 + i, \"tsunami\": 0},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n        \"id\": \"e\" + str(i),\n    })\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\nkept = [(r, m) for r, m in pairs if m is not None and m >= threshold]\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump(doc, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", str(threshold), path)\n    code_none, out_none, err_none = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", \"9\", path)\nprint(out)\nassert code == 0 and code_none == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert {r[0] for r in rows[1:]} == {r for r, _ in kept}\nassert sum(int(r[1]) for r in rows[1:]) == len(kept)\nassert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out_none))) == [[\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]]\n=== END AC regions-min-mag-and-empty ===\n\n=== AC regions-failure-contract ===\nIntent: A file that is not a FeatureCollection exits 1 and an unlisted option exits 2, each with empty standard output.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; `\",\"` without a following space does not split.\n- Ties in event count are broken by region name in byte order, not locale or case-insensitive order.\n- No region row is hardcoded; all values come from the file read.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Near.md ===\n# FEATURE: Near\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The `near` report: events within a haversine great-circle distance of a point, nearest first. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MagFilter.md, FEATURE-Formatting.md, FEATURE-Options.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes near, haversine_km |\n| Consumes    | read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, format_time, format_mag, format_decimal, parse_args |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes near --lat <deg> --lon <deg> --radius <km> [--min-mag <m>] <file>` lists the events whose distance from a point is at most the radius.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line. `--lat`, `--lon`, and `--radius` are all required. `parse_args` enforces `--lat` in -90..90, `--lon` in -180..180, and `--radius` greater than zero; any violation or omission is a usage error (exit 2).\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. `read_feed`, `extract_events`, and `filter_events` produce the kept events.\n2. `haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)` is a pure function on a sphere of radius 6371.0 km, with angles in radians:\n   `h = sin^2((lat2 - lat1) / 2) + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin^2((lon2 - lon1) / 2)` and `d = 2 * 6371.0 * asin(sqrt(h))`. Event coordinates are `[longitude, latitude, depth_km]`.\n3. `compute_near(events, lat, lon, radius)` keeps events whose unrounded distance is `<= radius` and orders them by unrounded distance ascending, then by event time ascending.\n4. `write_csv` writes the report, with `distance_km` rounded half up to one decimal.\n\n## Output\n\nHeader: `distance_km,time,mag,place,id`. One row per matching event: distance with one decimal, UTC time, magnitude with one decimal, place, id. An event at exactly the radius is included. No matches yields only the header with exit 0. Places containing commas are quoted by the `csv` module; non-ASCII places are UTF-8.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line.\n\n## Writes\n\nStandard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC near-haversine-distance-and-radius ===\nIntent: Reported distances match an independent haversine on a 6371.0 km sphere, and only events within the radius are listed, nearest first.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport tempfile\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dphi = p2 - p1\n    dlam = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin(dphi / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dlam / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))\n\n\norigin = (27.72, 85.32)\npoints = [\n    (\"far\", 35.68, 139.69),\n    (\"mid\", 28.60, 87.37),\n    (\"near1\", 28.80, 87.13),\n    (\"near2\", 28.50, 87.35),\n]\nfeatures = []\nfor i, (name, lat, lon) in enumerate(points):\n    features.append({\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0 + i / 10, \"place\": \"Place \" + name, \"time\": 1736200000000 + i * 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, 10.0]},\n        \"id\": name,\n    })\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}\ndist = {name: hav(origin[0], origin[1], lat, lon) for name, lat, lon in points}\nradius = round(sorted(dist.values())[2] + 1.0, 1)\ninside = sorted([n for n in dist if dist[n] <= radius], key=lambda n: dist[n])\nassert 0 < len(inside) < len(points)\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump(doc, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\n        \"near\", \"--lat\", str(origin[0]), \"--lon\", str(origin[1]), \"--radius\", str(radius), path\n    )\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"distance_km\", \"time\", \"mag\", \"place\", \"id\"]\nassert [r[4] for r in rows[1:]] == inside\nfor r in rows[1:]:\n    assert abs(float(r[0]) - dist[r[4]]) <= 0.051\n=== END AC BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Fetch.md ===\n# FEATURE: Fetch\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The `fetch` command: download a USGS date range as GeoJSON and save the response unchanged to a file. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-Options.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md, FEATURE-FeedValidation.md |\n| Provides    | quakes fetch, build_url, http_get |\n| Consumes    | parse_args, read_feed |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes fetch --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --end <YYYY-MM-DD> [--min-mag <m>] --out <file>` saves a period of the USGS event feed so the report commands can read it.\n\n## Trigger\n\nCommand line. `--start`, `--end`, and `--out` are required; `--min-mag` defaults to `2.5`. A missing required option, an unlisted option, or any positional argument is a usage error (exit 2) and no HTTP call is made.\n\n## Module layout\n\nCode lives in `cli/fetch.py`:\n\n- `build_url(start, end, min_mag) -> str` returns `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query` with query parameters `format=geojson`, `starttime=<start>`, `endtime=<end>`, `minmagnitude=<min_mag>`, `orderby=time-asc`. `min_mag` is the text given on the command line (or `2.5`).\n- `http_get(url) -> tuple[int, bytes]` is the single replaceable network function. It calls `urllib.request.urlopen` through attribute access on the `urllib.request` module (so a test can patch `urllib.request.urlopen`), returns the HTTP status and body bytes, and is the only function in the product that opens a connection.\n- The command handler calls `http_get` through the module global (`cli.fetch.http_get`) so tests can replace it.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Build the URL and call `http_get(url)`.\n2. Validate: status 200, body parses as JSON, and is an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a list `features` (reusing the `read_feed` validation rules on the body).\n3. Only after validation, write the body bytes unchanged (binary write) to `--out`.\n4. Write `fetched,<count>` to standard output, where `<count>` is the number of features.\n\nFailure handling is specified in FEATURE-FetchFailure.md.\n\n## Output\n\nStandard output is exactly one CSV line `fetched,<count>`; exit 0. The saved file is byte-for-byte the response body.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe USGS FDSN event web service over HTTPS.\n\n## Writes\n\nThe file named by `--out`, and standard output.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC fetch-saves-body-unchanged ===\nIntent: fetch writes the response body byte for byte to --out and prints fetched with the feature count; the HTTP call is stubbed.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nfeatures = [\n    {\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.1, \"place\": \"Awash, Ethiopia\", \"time\": 1735706358208, \"tsunami\": 0},\n     \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [40.0, 9.0, 10]}, \"id\": \"a\" + str(i)}\n    for i in range(3)\n]\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, indent=3, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\") + b\"\\n\\n\"\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert stub.call_count == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == body\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows == [[\"fetched\", str(len(features))]]\n=== END AC fetch-saves-body-unchanged ===\n\n=== AC fetch-request-url ===\nIntent: The request goes to the USGS FDSN query endpoint with the GeoJSON format, the given dates, the default minimum magnitude, and time ascending order.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.parse\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 0\n    url = stub.call_args[0][0]\nparts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)\nquery = urllib.parse.parse_qs(parts.query)\nassert parts.scheme == \"https\"\nassert parts.netloc == \"earthquake.usgs.gov\"\nassert parts.path == \"/fdsnws/event/1/query\"\nassert query[\"format\"] == [\"geojson\"]\nassert query[\"starttime\"] == [start]\nassert query[\"endtime\"] == [end]\nassert query[\"minmagnitude\"] == [\"2.5\"]\nassert query[\"orderby\"] == [\"time-asc\"]\n=== END AC fetch-request-url ===\n\n=== AC fetch-min-mag-passthrough ===\nIntent: An explicit --min-mag value is sent as minmagnitude, and build_url builds the same query directly.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.parse\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.fetch import build_url\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nstart = \"2025-02-01\"\nend = \"2025-02-03\"\nmin_mag = \"4.5\"\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)) as stub:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\n            \"fetch\", \"--min-mag\", min_mag, \"--end\", end, \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out_path\n        )\n    assert code == 0\n    url = stub.call_args[0][0]\nquery = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).query)\nassert query[\"minmagnitude\"] == [min_mag]\nassert query[\"starttime\"] == [start]\nassert query[\"endtime\"] == [end]\ndirect = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(build_url(start, end, min_mag)).query)\nassert direct == query\n=== END AC fetch-min-mag-passthrough ===\n\n=== AC fetch-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Missing required options, an unlisted option, or an extra positional argument exit 2, make no HTTP call, and write no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    cases = [\n        (\"fetch\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--out\", out_path),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path, \"extra\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", out_path, \"--n\", \"3\"),\n        (\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", \"--out\", out_path),\n    ]\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, b\"{}\")) as stub:\n        for args in cases:\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(*args)\n            assert code == 2, args\n            assert out == \"\", args\n        assert stub.call_count == 0\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-usage-errors ===\n\n=== AC fetch-http-get-uses-urllib ===\nIntent: http_get returns the status and body from urllib.request.urlopen, which is stubbed so no network connection is opened.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.fetch import http_get\n\npayload = b\"payload bytes\"\nstatus = 200\n\n\nclass FakeResponse:\n    def __init__(self, code, data):\n        self.status = code\n        self._data = data\n\n    def read(self):\n        return self._data\n\n    def getcode(self):\n        return self.status\n\n    def __enter__(self):\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *exc):\n        return False\n\n\nwith mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", return_value=FakeResponse(status, payload)) as opener:\n    got_status, got_body = http_get(\"https://example.invalid/query\")\nassert opener.call_count == 1\nassert got_status == status\nassert got_body == payload\n=== END AC fetch-http-get-uses-urllib ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Tests never open a network connection; every fetch test replaces `cli.fetch.http_get` or `urllib.request.urlopen`.\n- The saved file is the response body unchanged: no re-serialization, re-encoding, or newline translation.\n- The output file is written only after the response is validated.\n- Only the `fetch` command touches the network; report commands never do.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-FetchFailure.md ===\n# FEATURE: Fetch Failure\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Failure behavior of `fetch`: network, HTTP, and body errors exit 1 and never write or alter a file. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-Fetch.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | fetch failure handling |\n| Consumes    | http_get |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nWhen the download cannot produce a valid GeoJSON FeatureCollection, `fetch` reports an operational failure and leaves the filesystem exactly as it found it.\n\n## Trigger\n\nAny of the following during `quakes fetch` (after arguments parse successfully):\n\n- a network error (any `urllib.error.URLError`, `OSError`, or timeout from the HTTP layer);\n- an HTTP status other than 200;\n- a 200 body that is not JSON, or is JSON but not an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a list `features`.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- `http_get` returns `(status, body)` for every HTTP response, including non-200 statuses (an `HTTPError` is converted to its code and body), and raises `OperationalError` for `URLError`, `OSError`, and timeouts.\n- The `fetch` handler also converts any `OSError` raised by a replaced `http_get` into `OperationalError`.\n- A non-200 status or an invalid body raises `OperationalError`.\n- All checks complete before `--out` is opened, so no file is created and a pre-existing file at `--out` keeps its exact bytes.\n- The command exits 1, writes nothing to standard output, and writes one diagnostic line to standard error.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe HTTP response only.\n\n## Writes\n\nStandard error only; never the output file on failure.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-http-status ===\nIntent: A non-200 status exits 1 with empty standard output, one stderr line, and no file written.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nvalid = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}).encode(\"utf-8\")\nbad_status = 500\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(bad_status, valid)):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-http-status ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-bad-body ===\nIntent: A body that is not JSON, or JSON that is not a FeatureCollection, exits 1 and writes no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nbodies = [\n    b\"this is not json\",\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {}, \"geometry\": None}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": \"nope\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    json.dumps([1, 2, 3]).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n]\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    for n, body in enumerate(bodies):\n        out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved\" + str(n) + \".geojson\")\n        with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, body)):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n        assert code == 1, n\n        assert out == \"\", n\n        assert not os.path.exists(out_path), n\n=== END AC fetch-failure-bad-body ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-network-error ===\nIntent: A network error from a stubbed http_get, and a URLError from a patched urlopen, both exit 1 with no file written.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.error\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    first = os.path.join(tmp, \"first.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", side_effect=OSError(\"unreachable\")):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", first)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(first)\n\n    second = os.path.join(tmp, \"second.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", side_effect=urllib.error.URLError(\"no route\")) as opener:\n        code2, out2, err2 = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", second)\n    assert opener.call_count == 1\n    assert code2 == 1\n    assert out2 == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(second)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-network-error ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-http-error-status ===\nIntent: An HTTPError raised by urlopen is treated as a non-200 status, exits 1, and writes no file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport urllib.error\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nerror = urllib.error.HTTPError(\"https://example.invalid\", 503, \"unavailable\", {}, io.BytesIO(b\"down\"))\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", side_effect=error):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert not os.path.exists(out_path)\n=== END AC fetch-failure-http-error-status ===\n\n=== AC fetch-failure-preserves-existing-file ===\nIntent: A failed fetch leaves a pre-existing output file byte-for-byte untouched.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\noriginal = b\"previous contents, not JSON\\n\"\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    out_path = os.path.join(tmp, \"saved.geojson\")\n    with open(out_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        fh.write(original)\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(404, b\"missing\")):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == original\n    with mock.patch(\"cli.fetch.http_get\", return_value=(200, b\"not json\")):\n        code2, out2, err2 = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-02\", \"--out\", out_path)\n    assert code2 == 1\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == original\n=== END AC fetch-failure-preserves-existing-file ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- A failing `fetch` never creates, truncates, or modifies the output file.\n- A failing command writes nothing to standard output and exactly one diagnostic line to standard error; standard error text is never part of a contract.\n- Tests exercise failure only through stubbed HTTP; no test opens a network connection.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===","ttft_ms":32784,"type":"result","duration_ms":117589,"uuid":"64130898-9e22-46f4-bd81-8d0eecf69fdb","ttft_stream_ms":3922,"time_to_request_ms":166,"first_content_frame_ms":3923,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0,"model_usage_since_last_result":{"claude-sonnet-5-5":{"inputTokens":2,"outputTokens":20773,"cacheReadInputTokens":1568,"cacheCreationInputTokens":81543,"webSearchRequests":0,"costUSD":0.5340628000000001,"contextWindow":1000000,"maxOutputTokens":128000,"thinkingTokens":3758,"canonicalModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","provider":"firstParty","costBasis":"list"}}}
